cf.title: Migrate pg_commit_ts directory to the new node during an upgrade

input.subject: Patch for migration of the pg_commit_ts directory

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support, but the design depends on replication origin preservation that the thread has not settled. replication-ondisk-1 shows that the copied entries point at reassigned roident values when 0003 is dropped and patch 6743 is not committed. standards-compat-2 and standards-compat-1 show that the lasting meaning of --pg-commit-ts and the scope of the new hard error are undecided. These are fixable, but the list must agree on them before code review is useful.

brief.title: pg_upgrade: preserve pg_commit_ts commit timestamps in the new cluster
brief.problem: pg_upgrade does not copy the pg_commit_ts directory, so commit timestamps and their origin data are lost when track_commit_timestamp = on. The author's site uses commit times to find when rows changed, kept for up to 2 years, and copies the directory by hand today. Reviewers add a second use case: accurate logical replication conflict detection on an upgraded subscriber.
brief.proposed_design: pg_upgrade copies pg_commit_ts from the old cluster and passes the old oldest and newest commit-ts XIDs to pg_resetwal -c, where it used to pass next XID twice. In v16 the work is split: 0001 copies the directory, 0002 makes this opt-in with a new option, and 0003 saves and restores roident and remote_lsn of replication origins. A check fails the upgrade if the old cluster has commit-ts data but the new cluster has track_commit_timestamp off; v16 does not say whether this check stays once the option exists.
user_visible_surface: New pg_upgrade option --pg-commit-ts that turns on the copy; a reviewer proposed renaming it --preserve-commit-timestamps.
New pg_upgrade check step that fails with "track_commit_timestamp" must be "on" but is set to "off" on the new cluster.
Commit timestamps and origins, read by pg_xact_commit_timestamp_origin(), now survive pg_upgrade, which changes the documented note that they are not preserved.
0003 keeps replication origin roident values from the old cluster.
author_claims: The only cost is the time to copy the pg_commit_ts directory.
The patch does automatically what users do today by copying the directory and running pg_resetwal.
The author's site needs commit times for up to 2 years to find application errors.
Without the opt-in option, upgraded subscribers would log many update_origin_differs conflicts that did not appear before.
The option lets users who copy the directory with their own scripts keep doing so.
brief.thread_state: Kuroda now maintains a three-part v16. Maxim Orlov and Ajin Cherian say 0001 must not go in without 0002 or origin preservation, and Ajin asks to drop 0003 in favour of patch 6743, rename the option, and rebase.
unclear: The material does not say how pg_upgrade handles commit-ts entries that already exist in the new cluster, which Kuroda asked about and left open.
The material does not say whether the hard error on track_commit_timestamp = off stays once --pg-commit-ts exists.
Origins made with pg_replication_origin_create() are not migrated, and the material does not say whether that is in scope.
The material gives no measured copy time for a large pg_commit_ts directory.
The material does not say whether old clusters before 9.5, which have no commit timestamps, are handled or tested.

objections.title: Copied commit timestamps carry roident values the new cluster does not preserve
objections.failure_scenario: An admin upgrades a logical subscriber with --pg-commit-ts. Subscriptions get new roident values, so rows applied by one subscription are attributed to another, and pg_replication_origin_create() origins are not migrated at all. The apply worker logs false update_origin_differs conflicts, and audit queries on pg_xact_commit_timestamp_origin() return wrong origins.
objections.argument: Each commit_ts entry stores a roident, and message #37 shows that pg_upgrade reassigns roident values. 0002 makes the copy opt-in, but the copied data is still wrong for anyone who opts in while 0003 is dropped, as message #60 requests. Messages #59 and #60 tie safe use to patch 6743, which is not part of this proposal. Message #44 says manually created origins are not migrated.
objections.author_must_show: With 0003 dropped, what keeps the copied roident values pointing at the right origin, including origins made with pg_replication_origin_create()?

critic.reasoning: Message #37 reproduces the wrong attribution, and messages #59 and #60 agree the copy is safe for subscribers only with origin preservation. The opt-in option limits who is affected but does not make the copied roident values correct.

objections.title: Option described as temporary becomes a permanent command-line contract
objections.failure_scenario: Operators add --pg-commit-ts to their upgrade scripts. Once origin preservation lands, the project either keeps an option with no remaining purpose or removes it. If it is removed, those scripts fail on the next major version with an unknown-option error.
objections.argument: Message #46 calls the option a temporary solution to remove once an architecturally correct design exists. Message #57 says its side effects go away after patch 6743. Every pg_upgrade option in a release must be supported for later releases, so the long-term meaning of this option needs to be settled before it is added.
objections.author_must_show: Is --pg-commit-ts meant to stay once origins are preserved, and if so, what does it mean then?

critic.reasoning: Message #46 calls the option a temporary solution, and message #56 doubts it is needed. Message #57 names a lasting use, but the thread does not settle what the option means once origins are preserved.

objections.title: New hard error breaks existing upgrade scripts when commit timestamps are off
objections.failure_scenario: A site with track_commit_timestamp = on in the old cluster leaves it off in the new cluster, as it can today. After moving to the new pg_upgrade, the check step fails with "track_commit_timestamp" must be "on", even though the site never asked for timestamps to be copied. The site finds out during the upgrade window.
objections.argument: Message #11 added the check before the opt-in option existed, and message #37 asked for a warning instead, since copying is not mandatory. Message #44 then made copying opt-in. The brief says v16 does not state whether the check still fires without --pg-commit-ts. If it does, pg_upgrade rejects a setup it accepts today.
objections.author_must_show: Does the track_commit_timestamp check fire only when --pg-commit-ts is given, and what happens otherwise?

critic.reasoning: Message #57 suggests the author wants track_commit_timestamp = off to stay possible in the new cluster, but nothing in v16 says the check is skipped without --pg-commit-ts. The question is open and a new patch version can answer it.

objections.title: Option name describes a directory, not the behaviour users get
objections.failure_scenario: A user who wants commit timestamps after an upgrade searches the pg_upgrade options for "timestamp" or "preserve" and does not find --pg-commit-ts. The user upgrades without the option, and the timestamps are lost with no way to get them back.
objections.argument: Message #60 notes that the name and help text describe the implementation and proposes --preserve-commit-timestamps. The thread does not settle this. Message #60 also says the help line breaks the alphabetical order of the long options.
objections.author_must_show: Which name do pg_upgrade users understand without reading the source, and does the help text say what is preserved?

critic.reasoning: Message #60 raises the name and the thread has no reply yet. The help text "copy pg_commit_ts directory" does not say what is preserved, so the user interface concern stands; the alphabetical order point is polish and adds no weight.

objections.title: Without origin preservation, the shippable part serves mainly one site's audit use
objections.failure_scenario: 0001 and 0002 are committed and patch 6743 is not. Logical replication users leave --pg-commit-ts off to avoid false update_origin_differs conflicts, so the conflict-detection use case gains nothing. The new option then serves mainly sites that use commit timestamps as a change-time history, like the author's.
objections.argument: The only field report is the author's site, which keeps commit times for up to two years to find application errors (message #42). Kuroda asked for a stronger use case (message #41), and Sawada's non-replication example is hypothetical (message #39). Amit asked what value the patch has without origins (message #38), and messages #57, #59 and #60 agree the option exists because origins are not yet preserved. Users who need the history can copy the directory and run pg_resetwal today (message #2), and the author calls that unreliable but still uses it.
objections.author_must_show: Apart from your own site, which users rely on commit timestamps surviving an upgrade without logical replication, and is that enough to justify this before origins are preserved?

critic.reasoning: One claim is too strong: message #30 shows conflict detection for locally changed rows works after the copy without origin preservation. The only field report is still the author's site (message #42), and message #41 asked for a stronger use case.

refuted.title: Raw copy freezes the commit_ts SLRU layout across major versions
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release changes the commit_ts entry or segment layout, for example wider XIDs or a wider origin id. pg_upgrade still copies the old files byte for byte. The new server reads the old pages with the new layout and returns wrong timestamps or origins, and nobody notices until a user queries them.
refuted.argument: pg_commit_ts can change between major versions today because pg_upgrade drops it. Copying pg_xact and pg_multixact already means any format change there needs a conversion step in pg_upgrade. The proposal adds a third SLRU to that duty. It does not add a version guard or say who writes the converter when the layout changes.
refuted.author_must_show: What makes pg_upgrade refuse the copy or convert it when the commit_ts on-disk layout differs between the old and new major versions?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future layout change that no one has proposed. pg_upgrade already copies pg_xact and pg_multixact under the same duty, so the proposal follows existing practice.

refuted.title: A temporary pg_upgrade option would become permanent
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator puts --pg-commit-ts into upgrade scripts in the first release. Once origins are preserved and the false conflicts go away, removing the option breaks those scripts. So pg_upgrade keeps an option that only marks a past workaround, and its relation to the hard track_commit_timestamp check is still not defined.
refuted.argument: Message #46 describes the option as "a temporary solution that will be removed after creating an architecturally correct solution." Message #57 makes the same point, and Kuroda doubts the option is needed (message #56). Removing a pg_upgrade switch is a compatibility break, and message #60 notes the name describes the implementation. The brief also records that v16 does not say whether the pg_fatal on track_commit_timestamp = off stays once the option exists.
refuted.author_must_show: Once origin preservation is committed, should commit timestamps be preserved by default, and if so, what would --pg-commit-ts still be for?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Its extra points about the check and the option name are covered by standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-3.

refuted.title: Commit-ts copy is correct only after a separate patch lands
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes 0001 and 0002 while patch 6743 is still in review. A user with subscriptions runs pg_upgrade with the option, and roident values are reassigned. Apply workers then log update_origin_differs conflicts that point at the wrong subscription, and the user sees these only in the server log after replication restarts.
refuted.argument: Message #37 shows that copied commit-ts entries point at reassigned origins. Message #59 explains that 0001 widens the valid commit-ts XID range, so lookups that used to fail now succeed with stale roident values. Message #49 says the origin patch "may have to be pushed first", and message #60 asks to drop 0003. If 0003 is dropped and 6743 is delayed, nothing in the proposal stops users from hitting this, apart from the documentation.
refuted.author_must_show: If 0003 is dropped and patch 6743 is not yet committed, what stops pg_upgrade from copying commit timestamps that reference reassigned origins?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same stale roident problem and also covers origins made with pg_replication_origin_create().

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade copies the pg_commit_ts SLRU files and sets the commit-ts XID range with pg_resetwal -c.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Copied entries carry roident values that logical replication conflict detection reads on an upgraded subscriber.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: 0003 restores roident and remote_lsn of replication origins in the new cluster.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: New hard error breaks existing upgrade scripts when commit timestamps are off

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new pg_upgrade option, described in message #46 as temporary, and a new check step must be supported in later releases.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: see objection demand-1: Without origin preservation, the shippable part serves mainly one site's audit use

questions: With 0003 dropped and patch 6743 not yet committed, what keeps copied roident values pointing at the right origin, including origins made with pg_replication_origin_create()?
Should this patch wait for patch 6743, or is it meant to be committed before origin preservation exists?
Once origins are preserved, does --pg-commit-ts stay, and what does it mean then?
Does the track_commit_timestamp check fire only when --pg-commit-ts is given, and what happens to existing upgrades otherwise?
What does pg_upgrade do with commit-ts entries that already exist in the new cluster before the copy?

committability.owner_note: The review notes record committer support for the logical replication use case in messages #27 and #38. The owner would need to know pg_upgrade and replication origins.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a third SLRU that pg_upgrade copies across major versions, for a pg_upgrade option that scripts will depend on, and for correct origin attribution on upgraded subscribers. None of these has an end date.
committability.author_follow_up: The original author still takes part late in the thread (messages #42, #46, #57), and a reviewer now maintains the v16 patch set. The CommitFest entry needs a rebase as of 2026-11-10.

priority.reason: The feature helps sites that run with track_commit_timestamp = on, mainly logical replication subscribers and audit users like the author's site. The patch is small, but its correctness depends on the open origin preservation question and on the lasting meaning of the new option.

provisional_note: Only the first 3 of 60 messages and no v16 code were read. This review could not check how the copy sets the commit-ts XID range, how it treats existing entries in the new cluster, or how it handles old clusters before 9.5.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: add timing information to pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the elapsed time of each pg_upgrade step to the status output, for example "ok (took 82 ms)", formatted like psql's PrintTiming(). The goal was to show where upgrade time goes and to measure future work on reducing pg_upgrade downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned who besides developers would use the timings and said pg_upgrade output already has too much information that users cannot act on. He suggested that shell tools such as "pg_upgrade | ts" or "ts -i" are enough, and the author agreed to leave it at that unless someone saw a reason to build it in. Only a related fix that raised MESSAGE_WIDTH to 62 was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's just for developers and expert users, perhaps existing
shell-level functionality like "pg_upgrade | ts" would suffice?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch for pg_upgrade explained what "compatible initdb flags" means for the new cluster: the same encoding, locale and checksum settings as the old one. It told users to find the encoding and locale of template0 with psql -l and the checksum setting with pg_controldata.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
A better way to get the
*cluster* locale is from pg_controldata.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade version and path checking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes pg_upgrade check every executable it uses, require the new binaries to match pg_upgrade's exact major and minor version, and default --new-bindir to pg_upgrade's own directory. It came from Tom Lane's report that pg_upgrade 11.3 would use pg_dump 11.1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed 0002 to 0004, which add the executable checks, the --new-bindir default and a typo fix. He found that 0001 compares pg_upgrade's version only with pg_ctl's, so it does not make all binaries match, and proposed a version check for each validate_exec() call instead. On 2019-09-02 the author said a new version would come that week, but no later version appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It compares (new_cluster.bin_version != PG_VERSION_NUM), but new_cluster.bin_version is actually just the version of pg_ctl, so this is just comparing the version of pg_upgrade with the version of pg_ctl, which is not wrong, but doesn't really achieve the full goal of having all binaries match.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Pass -j option down to vacuumdb
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_upgrade pass its -j option to the vacuumdb commands in the generated analyze_new_cluster.sh script, so the post-upgrade analyze runs in parallel. Later versions added a VACUUM_OPTS variable to the script and a suggested vacuumdb --jobs command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that pg_upgrade -j and vacuumdb -j are bound by different resources, so the same value should not be reused, and the generated script is meant to analyze gently. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier did not see most of the patch as better than the status quo and preferred a printed hint or a documentation-only change. The thread then moved to copying statistics in pg_upgrade instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So based on that linking the value used by pg_upgrade and vacuumdb is a bad concept in my opinion, and the patch should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Preserve versions of initdb-created collations in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_upgrade preserve the recorded versions of collations created by initdb. In binary-upgrade mode, pg_dump would delete all initdb-created collations in the new cluster and dump CREATE COLLATION commands with version information, instead of updating the existing objects in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review showed that the patch makes the pg_upgrade check fail for clusters initialized with SQL_ASCII encoding, where ICU collations for that encoding do not exist, and that it leaves the recreated collations looking like user-defined objects. The author then questioned the approach and suggested not creating collations in initdb at all. The reviewer replied that the problem would go away if the separate per-object collation version patch set were committed, since that drops the collversion column. The author then marked the patch Returned with Feedback without further changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this problem goes away if we commit the per-object collation
version patch set[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Backport perl tests for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Backport the Perl TAP version of the pg_upgrade tests (commit 322becb60) and related follow-up commits to REL_13_STABLE and REL_14_STABLE, replacing test.sh there. The goal was zero dump differences in cross-version upgrade tests, so users would not need to compare dumps by eye.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the TAP tests were new development that took several tries to get right on HEAD, so backporting them risks a test bug that hides a critical pg_upgrade issue. He preferred to keep further work on HEAD only, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we were to backport
any of this, there is a risk of introducing a bug in what we do with
any of that, potentially hiding a issue critical related to
pg_upgrade.  That's not worth taking a risk for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve documentation for pg_upgrade, standbys and rsync
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the pg_upgrade documentation for upgrading standbys with rsync: it recommends rsync --relative, updates the version numbers and paths in the examples, and adds a reminder to create standby.signal. Later versions also add SQL steps to drop leftover temporary tables and truncate unlogged tables before the rsync, and reorder the preparation steps.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost argued that this procedure is too hard to get right in an rsync command or a documented procedure, and that a tool should replace it. He proposed moving the text out of the documentation to a wiki. Robert Haas found the new order of the preparation steps confusing. The author saw no agreement and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
To be more explicit though- we should write a tool to do this.  We
shouldn't try to document a way to do it because it's hard to get right.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert ill-considered change in pg_resetwal output.
Reverted commit(s): Use the terminology "WAL file" not "log file" more consistently.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 31dcfae83 changed one pg_resetwal output string, and a
corresponding test in pg_upgrade, without sufficient thought for
the consequences.  We can't change that output without creating
hazards for cross-version upgrades, since pg_upgrade needs to be able
to read the output of several different versions of pg_resetwal.
There may well be external tools with the same requirement.

For the moment, just revert those two changes.  What we really
ought to do here is have a separate, stable, easily machine-readable
output format for pg_resetwal and pg_controldata, as proposed
years ago by Alvaro.  Once that's in place and tools no longer
need to depend on the exact spelling of the human-readable output,
we can put back this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
Reverted commit(s): Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 06f5295 as per issues with this approach, both in
terms of efficiency impact and stability.  First, contrary to the
single-item cache for transaction IDs in transam.c, the cache may finish
by not be hit for a long time, and without an invalidation mechanism to
clear it, it would cause inconsistent results on wraparound for
example.  Second, the use of SubTransGetTopmostTransaction() for the
caching has a limited impact on performance.  SubTransGetParent() could
have more impact, though the benchmarking of the single-item approach
still needs to be proved, particularly under the conditions where SLRU
lookups are stressed in parallel with overflowed snapshots (aka more
than 64 subxids generated, for example).

After discussion with Andres Freund.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P7] and [P17] touch pg_upgrade's handling of control data and pg_resetwal, but neither recorded reason applies: this patch sets the commit-ts XID range explicitly and reads existing pg_controldata lines without changing any output. No message in the thread cites an earlier attempt; message #2 says it is not known why pg_upgrade never copied pg_commit_ts, and patch 6743 is a parallel proposal, not a rejection.

Kuroda's question about overwriting commit_ts entries in the new cluster seems minor: pg_upgrade already replaces pg_xact wholesale, and post-restore XIDs fall outside the copied range. The standby rsync procedure was not checked.

This proposal has no new privilege or exposure aspect. pg_upgrade runs as the cluster owner, and the commit timestamps it keeps were already readable through pg_xact_commit_timestamp_origin() in the old cluster, so no role gains access it did not have before. The SQL that 0003 generates from old-cluster origin data was rejected in message #45, and message #60 asks to drop 0003, so that concern is already settled in the thread.

The hot-path cost is limited to pg_upgrade run time, and only when the option is given. No measured copy time is shown. The listed precedents touch pg_upgrade and pg_resetwal, but their recorded reasons do not apply here.

The only existing alternative is the undocumented manual idiom from message #2: copy pg_commit_ts and run pg_resetwal -c with XIDs read from pg_controldata, which the author calls unreliable in message #42. Origin preservation for subscribers has no supported manual path, and the overlap of 0003 with patch 6743 is already being handled in the thread, so nothing is raised from this angle.
The logical replication use case has committer support (messages #27, #38), but it depends on origin preservation from patch 6743. For that case alone, demand is not in doubt.
